scenarios.name: identical_distributions
scenarios.findings: Two samples from the same normal(100,10) should show no evidence of a shift and a negligible effect size.

scenarios.name: clearly_shifted_distributions
scenarios.findings: A 3-sigma shift (normal(100,10) vs normal(130,10)) should be detected with a small p-value and a large effect size.

scenarios.name: same_effect_different_sample_size
scenarios.detail: n=20: cliffs_delta=-0.490 CI_width=12.950 | n=400: cliffs_delta=-0.309 CI_width=2.854 (want similar delta, narrower CI at n=400)
scenarios.findings: The same underlying 5-unit mean shift should produce a similar Cliff's Delta at n=20 and n=400, but a visibly narrower bootstrap CI at n=400 -- sample size buys precision, not a bigger effect.

scenarios.name: outlier_heavy_distribution
scenarios.detail: mean shift=4496.9 (want >1000, outlier-driven), median shift=0.126 (want <1, outlier-robust), cliffs_delta=-0.0269 magnitude=negligible (want not large)
scenarios.findings: Injecting 3 extreme outliers into a 100-point sample should distort the mean drastically while leaving the median and the rank-based effect size largely unaffected -- exactly why this project prefers percentile/rank statistics for latency data.

scenarios.name: known_bootstrap_case
scenarios.detail: 95% CI=[48.726, 51.249] for true mean=50.0 (want true mean inside the interval)
scenarios.findings: A 2000-point sample from Uniform(0,100) has a true mean of exactly 50; the bootstrap CI for the sample mean should contain it.

scenarios.name: deterministic_analysis_seed
scenarios.detail: run1={Estimate:99.9637933044906 Lower:98.13536104316799 Upper:102.00941848326568 Confidence:0.95 NResamples:2000 SampleSize:100} run2={Estimate:99.9637933044906 Lower:98.13536104316799 Upper:102.00941848326568 Confidence:0.95 NResamples:2000 SampleSize:100} (want identical)
scenarios.findings: Same data + same analysis seed must produce the exact same bootstrap confidence interval, every time.
